title: Publishing to many never-subscribed topics creates empty global topic keys
source: MQTT PUBLISH with attacker-controlled distinct fixed topicName, retain=false is sufficient
sink: PublishProtocol always calls topicRegistry.getSubscribesByTopic; FixedTopicFilter.getSubscribeByTopic uses topicChannels.computeIfAbsent(topic, ...)
retention: empty CopyOnWriteArraySet entries are stored in FixedTopicFilter.topicChannels and no cleanup path removes entries created only by publish lookup
bound: messageMaxSize bounds topic string length per frame; no total topic key quota or negative-cache eviction found
impact: an unauthenticated client can grow broker heap with tiny PUBLISH packets even when no subscribers and retain=false. This is a default external request path and more clearly application-specific than generic connection flooding.
static_trigger_shape: CONNECT anonymously, then publish tiny QoS0 non-retained messages to unique fixed topics such as dos/empty/{i}; no subscriber setup is required.
scope_notes: No disk storage and no special config; dynamic proof still required for service-unavailability threshold.
